intro: Look up at Hoşap Castle, south of Van, in Van province. Its story runs from the 9th century BC to the 17th century AD, and what you see is the magnificent castle of the 17th-century Mahmudi principality.
history: This rock was already occupied in Urartian times. Centuries later, in the 17th century, Sarı Süleyman Bey of the Mahmudi tribe rebuilt it. The result is among the finest surviving examples of Ottoman-Van architecture.
structure-1: You are now before Hoşap Castle itself, the magnificent castle built south of Van by the Mahmudi principality in the 17th century. Take a moment to follow its walls as they climb the rock.
structure-2: Here is the Sarıkaya Mansion, a summer mansion cut into the rock within Hoşap Castle. Imagine the cool shade it offered in the heat of summer.
structure-4: You are standing at the Castle Gate, the monumental entrance of the fortress. Every visitor, friend or foe, had to pass this way.
structure-5: Now the Inner Courtyard: the innermost court, where a fortress's defences were strongest. This was the heart that every wall around you was built to protect.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Urartian Inscription.
facts: Did you know? The Persian inscription on the castle gate reads 'there is nothing like it in the world'. The castle was built in 1643 by Sarı Süleyman, bey of the Mahmudi, and as it wraps a whole rock outcrop it is one of the most theatrical castles in Anatolia. And a darker tale: the story goes that the bey had the architect's hand cut off, so that its like could never be built again.
outro: This brings our journey through Hoşap Castle to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this castle keep watch for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
